title: Image height inverts back to the angle
quantity: largest |θ − θ(r(θ))| over each projection's field, every base projection and every built-in lens's Kannala–Brandt curve
reference: the identity: θ(r) is the inverse of r(θ) (closed form, or Newton's method for Kannala–Brandt)

title: Radial sampling dr/dθ
quantity: largest relative difference of dr/dθ from a central finite difference of r(θ), every base projection and built-in lens
reference: a central difference of r(θ) with step 10⁻⁶ rad

title: Rectilinear lens against OpenCV's pinhole projection
quantity: largest pixel distance between Intrinsics.project_dirs and cv2.projectPoints for directions over the image, with a pixel aspect of 1.004 and an offset principal point
reference: OpenCV cv2.projectPoints (no distortion); OpenCV pixel centres are at integers, Vantage's at i + ½

title: Kannala–Brandt lenses against OpenCV's fisheye model
quantity: largest pixel distance between Intrinsics.project_dirs and cv2.fisheye.projectPoints (D = k1…k4) for every built-in lens, directions up to 88° off the axis
reference: OpenCV cv2.fisheye.projectPoints: θ_d = θ(1 + k1θ² + k2θ⁴ + k3θ⁶ + k4θ⁸), the same model

title: Pixel to ray against OpenCV's fisheye undistortion
quantity: largest angle between Intrinsics.unproject's ray and the ray cv2.fisheye.undistortPoints gives for the same pixel, every built-in lens, pixels up to 75° off the axis
reference: OpenCV cv2.fisheye.undistortPoints (iterated to 10⁻¹⁴)

title: Built-in lenses reproduce e-con's stated field of view
quantity: largest difference between a built-in lens model's horizontal, vertical and diagonal field (limited by its image circle) and the field e-con states for it
reference: the FOV e-con Systems publishes for each lens (H, V, D)

title: Pixel density on a target facing the camera
quantity: largest relative difference between Intrinsics.density_px_per_cm and the square root of the pixel area a 1 mm square facing the camera at 1 m covers (its corners projected through the lens), from the axis to the edge of each lens's field
reference: the projected area of a small square, by the shoelace formula

title: A rectilinear camera looking straight down at a plate
quantity: share of footprint cells the analysis marks differently from the rectangle the image casts on the plate (4h²·tan α_h·tan α_v); the largest relative difference of a seen cell's pixel density from f / (p·cos^1.5 θ) / R; cells differing away from the rectangle's edges must be none
reference: the pyramid of a pinhole camera cut by a plane, written out in the check

title: An aimed and rolled camera's footprint on a plate
quantity: share of footprint cells the analysis marks differently from the quadrilateral the image corners of a rectilinear camera at yaw 30°, pitch 50° down and roll 8° cast on the plate (rays built from the documented ISO 8855 Z-Y-X convention with scipy, not the app's rotations); the largest relative density difference as for the downward camera; cells differing away from the edges must be none
reference: the image corners' rays intersected with the plane, written out in the check

title: A fisheye's image circle on a plate is a disc
quantity: share of cells the analysis marks differently from the disc of radius h·tan θ_max a downward equidistant lens's image circle (inside the sensor) casts; the largest relative difference of a seen cell's density from (f/p)·√(θ / sin θ) / R
reference: the cone of the image circle cut by the plane, written out in the check

title: Cube maps against exact ray casting
quantity: share of random directions from each camera of the project in which the occlusion cube map (body and rig, 256 × 256 texels per face) and an exact ray cast against the same triangles disagree on whether the body is hit; every disagreement must lie within 1° of the exact silhouette
reference: Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection against every occluder triangle, written for the check

title: Cube-map depth against exact ray casting
quantity: share of the texels where a camera's cube map (body and rig, 256 × 256 texels per face) is hit whose stored depth is more than 0.1 % off the exact first hit along the texel's centre ray and more than 5 % off every exact hit within one texel of it (rays through the neighbouring texels' centres and the texel's edges): the depth must be exact but for the texel's own size
reference: Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection against every occluder triangle, written for the check

title: Which ground points a camera sees past the body
quantity: share of ground points of the region of interest in each camera's image whose visibility (analysis.eval_points with the cube map) differs from an exact test of the straight line from the lens to the point against every occluder triangle (with the same 2 cm + 1 % distance allowance); every disagreement must lie within 1° of the exact silhouette
reference: Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection along the line of sight, written for the check

title: Object pixels through a pinhole lens
quantity: largest relative difference of an object's pixel height and width (perception.object_pixels) from f·H/Z and f·W/Z for a level 6 mm pinhole camera, objects on and off the axis and a sign on a post
reference: the pinhole projection of a fronto-parallel segment, f·H/Z with Z the depth along the axis

title: Object pixels through a fisheye follow its local sampling
quantity: largest relative difference of an object's pixel height and width through the built-in H05R2 lens, 30 m out on the axis and 55° off it, from its size over the distance times the lens's local sampling (radial dr/dθ, tangential r/sin θ)
reference: the first-order local magnification of the lens at the object's direction

title: Perception range of a pinhole camera
quantity: relative difference of the far range ahead the study finds for a car with a level 6 mm rectilinear camera on the sample's front bumper from the range where the car is exactly min_px tall, f·H / min_px (measured from the vehicle centre), for min_px 20 and 33
reference: the pinhole relation f·H/Z = min_px solved for Z

title: Critical-target pixels through a pinhole lens
quantity: largest relative difference of a 1.7 m × 0.5 m pedestrian's pixel height and width 10 m ahead of a level 4 mm pinhole camera, and of its distance, from f·h/Z, f·w/Z and the straight-line distance
reference: the pinhole projection, written out in the check

title: Mounting envelopes of a pinhole camera
quantity: largest difference of the single-axis pitch and yaw limits the envelope search finds from where the target's top, feet or outer columns leave the image (half the field minus their angle), and of the backward x limit from where its height falls to min_px (in metres × 100, so 0.02 is 0.2 mm)
reference: the angles of the target's edges against the half field, and f·h / min_px, written out in the check

title: Ground rings of a level lidar
quantity: largest relative difference of each channel's ground ring radius (sensors.ground_rings) from h / tan|ε| for every downward channel of the OS1-128 2 m above the ground; the front of a ring of a lidar pitched 5° down must lie at h / tan(|ε| + 5°) (to the 1° azimuth sampling)
reference: the cone of a beam at elevation ε cut by the ground plane, written out in the check

title: Points a level lidar puts on the ground
quantity: relative difference of the points per frame summed over the ground density map (lidar and radar coverage) from every downward channel within range times the columns per revolution, a level OS1-128 2 m up with nothing in the way and a map that holds every ring; the nearest ground point in every direction must be the lowest ring
reference: the beam count: channels reaching the ground within range × columns per revolution

title: Lidar points on an object: a level lidar
quantity: largest relative difference between the points per frame the coverage study counts on a car (1.5 m × 1.8 m) 8–60 m from an OS1-128 2 m up, ahead and 35° to the side, and the beams that meet the car's face when every beam of a revolution is cast, averaged over 16 phases of the scan's azimuths (one phase differs by up to a point per channel); the channels crossing the car must agree within one
reference: every beam (channel elevation × column azimuth, through the lidar's rotation) intersected with a vertical rectangle square to the line of sight, written for the check

title: Lidar points on an object: a lidar pitched 5° down
quantity: largest relative difference between the points per frame the coverage study counts on a car (1.5 m × 1.8 m) 8–60 m from an OS1-128 2 m up, ahead and 35° to the side, and the beams that meet the car's face when every beam of a revolution is cast, averaged over 16 phases of the scan's azimuths (one phase differs by up to a point per channel); the lidar pitched 5° down
reference: every beam (channel elevation × column azimuth, through the lidar's rotation) intersected with a vertical rectangle square to the line of sight, written for the check

title: Radar range against the cross-section
quantity: largest relative difference of the pedestrian's and cyclist's radar range from the car's scaled by (σ / σ_car)^¼, and of the car's from the zone's 100 m (slant to its centre), a corner radar with nothing in the way
reference: the radar equation: received power ∝ σ / R⁴, so the range at a fixed threshold ∝ σ^¼

title: One fascia layer against the sum of its reflections
quantity: largest difference of the power reflectance and transmittance of a single dielectric slab (materials.stack_rt, the characteristic-matrix method) from the sum of its internal bounces, TE and TM, lossless and lossy, normal to 75° incidence at 76.5 GHz
reference: the Airy summation of the slab's multiple reflections with the Fresnel interface coefficients, written for the check

title: Layer identities: half wave, quarter wave, Brewster, energy
quantity: largest deviation from the closed forms: a lossless half-wave layer transmits everything; a quarter-wave layer reflects ((n²−1)/(n²+1))²; TM at Brewster's angle tan θ_B = n is not reflected; a lossless four-layer stack (substrate, primer, basecoat, clear coat) keeps R + T = 1 from 0° to 85°
reference: thin-film closed forms (Macleod; Born & Wolf)

title: A painted bumper plate against a measurement
quantity: distance of the modelled 77 GHz one-way transmission |S21| of a 3.416 mm talc-filled PP plate with the library's primer, a metallic basecoat (ε = 48.94, 15 µm) and a 40 µm clear coat, for substrate ε 2.9–3.1, from the range of Emilsson's two measurements of the plate (−2.34 and −1.98 dB); |S11| must lie within 0.9 dB of its measured range (−5.75 to −4.86 dB)
reference: Emilsson's measured S21 and S11 of the painted plate (sample 11)

title: A radar behind the bumper fascia loses range by the radar equation
quantity: relative difference of the long-range radar RD1's range on a car straight ahead (from the vehicle centre), moved 8 cm behind the sample's front bumper fascia, from where the car's centre lies 250 m × 10^(−L/40) from the radar, L the two-way loss the materials study gives for that zone
reference: the radar equation (range ∝ (two-way power transmission)^¼) applied to the materials study's loss, the geometry written out in the check

title: Cross-section of a trihedral corner reflector
quantity: relative difference of observability.reflector_rcs from 4πa⁴ / 3λ² at 77 GHz for edges of 50–300 mm
reference: the peak RCS of a triangular trihedral (Knott et al.)

title: A ray through a glass plate shifts by the plate formula
quantity: largest relative difference of the sideways shift materials.glass_optics gives for 3.5 mm side glass (n 1.52) from d·sin θ·(1 − cos θ / √(n² − sin²θ)), 0–75° incidence, and of the windscreen's slide along its surface from Σ d_j (tan θ − sin θ_j / cos θ_j)
reference: the textbook lateral displacement of a plane-parallel plate (Hecht)

title: Glass transmission and reflection conserve energy
quantity: largest |R + T − 1| of a non-absorbing glass (n 1.5) from 0° to 85° (incoherent slab, Fresnel at both faces), and the difference of a class's transmission at normal incidence from its stated visible transmission
reference: energy conservation, and the class's own t_vis

title: Rain attenuation coefficients against ITU-R P.838-3
quantity: largest difference of weather.p838's k_H, α_H, k_V and α_V (the recommendation's curve fits, eqs. 2–3 and Tables 1–4) from its Table 5 at 16 frequencies from 1 to 1000 GHz, in units of half the last printed digit
reference: Recommendation ITU-R P.838-3, Table 5, as printed

title: Fog attenuation at radar frequencies (ITU-R P.840)
quantity: largest relative difference of weather.liquid_water_coefficient (P.840's K_l from its double-Debye permittivity) from the Rayleigh absorption of small water drops computed from the complex permittivity directly, (6π/λ)·Im(−(ε−1)/(ε+2)), at 24, 77 and 100 GHz and 0–20 °C
reference: Rayleigh absorption by drops much smaller than the wavelength, from the same Debye permittivity, written out in the check

title: Optical rain and snow attenuation against ITU-R P.1814
quantity: largest relative difference of the optical rain attenuation (1–100 mm/h) and the wet and dry snow attenuation (0.5–10 mm/h at 550, 905 and 1550 nm) from P.1814's Table 2 (France: k 1.076, α 0.67) and Table 3 as printed
reference: Recommendation ITU-R P.1814, Tables 2 and 3

title: Contrast extinction (Koschmieder) and the meteorological optical range
quantity: largest relative difference of the visible extinction for fog of MOR 50 m–10 km from −ln 0.05 / MOR, of the distance at which contrast C0 falls to ε from ln(C0/ε)/σ (residual of C0·e^(−σd) = ε), and of the extinction away from 550 nm from Kim's (λ / 550 nm)^−q
reference: Koschmieder's law with WMO's 5 % contrast threshold; Kim et al.'s q(V)

title: Lidar and radar range in extinction (Lambert W)
quantity: largest relative difference of weather.lidar_range (R·e^(αR) = R_c, solved with Lambert's W) and weather.radar_range (R⁴·e^(2aR) = R_c⁴) from a bracketing root finder on the same equations
reference: scipy.optimize.brentq on the defining equations

title: The headlamp pattern meets UN R112
quantity: largest shortfall, as a share of the requirement, of the typical low-beam pattern's intensity at R112's class B test points (minimums 75R, 50R, 50V, 25L, 25R and zone IV; maximums 50L, 75L, B50L, BR and zone I below twice the 50R/75R), and of the high beam (I_max 40 500–215 000 cd, ±2.5° and ±5°)
reference: UN Regulation No. 112, class B photometric requirements

title: The camera's minimum luminance from its photon budget
quantity: relative difference of the electrons per cd/m² weather.camera_floor gives from π·T/(4N²)·t·Φ·A·QE, and of the signal-to-noise ratio at its L_min from snr_min (S / √(S + read noise²)), STURDeCAM31 with H05R2
reference: the photon budget of a pixel behind a lens of f-number N (Janesick), written out in the check

title: Headlamp illuminance: inverse square, cosine and extinction
quantity: largest relative difference of weather.illuminance at a point 20 m ahead from I/d², from I·cos(i)/d² on a surface tilted 60° away, and from E_ambient + I·e^(−σd)/d² in fog
reference: the photometric inverse-square law with Lambert's cosine and Beer–Lambert extinction

title: Sun position against the SPA paper's worked example
quantity: largest difference of the topocentric zenith angle and azimuth exposure.sun_at gives for Golden, Colorado, 2003-10-17 12:30:30 local time (UTC−7), from Reda & Andreas' 50.11162° and 194.34024°
reference: I. Reda and A. Andreas, NREL Solar Position Algorithm, worked example

title: Solar coordinates against Meeus's worked examples
quantity: largest difference of the sun's declination, right ascension and apparent longitude (degrees), distance (AU × 100) and equation of time (minutes / 10) at 1992 October 13.0 from Meeus's examples 25.a and 28.b; and of the noon elevation 90° − |φ − δ| (no refraction) at two latitudes
reference: J. Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, examples 25.a and 28.b; spherical astronomy at solar noon

title: Static loads against hand calculations
quantity: largest relative difference of the corner drops, the tyre forces, the pitch and the roll the static solve gives from hand calculations: a load over the front axle (each front corner W/2 on its spring and tyre in series, pitch atan(drop / L)); a load to the left, with and without an anti-roll bar (heave W/4 on the series rate, ±W·y/(2T) per wheel on the wheel rate plus the bar, roll atan(2a / T)); a bump stop beyond its gap (gap + (F − k·gap)/(k + k_bump))
reference: springs in series, force and moment balance, written out in the check

title: The static solve balances force and moments
quantity: largest relative residual of the vertical force and of the moments about x and y (Σ tyre forces against Σ weights) and of the four corners' drops from one plane, for 12 random sets of loads on typical corners with a measured load–travel curve at one corner
reference: static equilibrium of a rigid body on four supports

title: Brake dive and cornering roll against hand calculations
quantity: largest relative difference of the corner drops and the pitch under 0.8 g braking (with 0, 30/10 and 100 % anti-dive/anti-lift: the linkage takes its share of ΔF = M·a·h/L off the springs) and of the drops and the roll at 0.5 g lateral (roll centres 0 and 0.2 m, anti-roll bar 0 and 12 N/mm: the geometric share M/2·a·rc/T through the links, the elastic share on the springs and bar), unsprung masses zero
reference: quasi-static load transfer with anti-dive and roll centres (Gillespie; Milliken), written out in the check

title: Road primitives against their definitions
quantity: largest difference of the road height (ramp, crest and sag vertical curves, garage ramp, speed bump, kerbs, crowned road) from its definition written out again, and of its gradient from central differences away from the kinks, at 400 random points per primitive
reference: each primitive's closed form (a vertical curve is the parabola of a grade changing linearly with distance) and a central difference with step 10⁻⁵ m

title: Seeing the road past its own crests and kerbs
quantity: share of road points (3000 per camera position, four positions, the primitives together) whose visibility the ray march (terrain.clear) decides differently from a dense brute-force march of 4000 samples per line of sight
reference: a brute-force march along every line of sight, written for the check

title: The road hidden beyond a crest
quantity: difference of where the sample's front camera loses sight of the road beyond a crest (radius 250 m, falling to −10 %, 6 m ahead of the bumper; terrain.profile) from where the line from the lens tangent to the crest's parabola meets it (s² + 2as − 2Rz = 0)
reference: the tangent from the camera to the vertical curve, written out in the check

title: The horizon in a rectilinear camera
quantity: largest difference of the horizon row loadcases.horizon_at gives from c_y − f·tan(pitch) for camera and body pitches between −2° and 35°, and of its tilt from the roll (rolls ±2–3°)
reference: the vanishing line of the ground plane in a pinhole camera, written out in the check

title: When the lidar sweep crosses each camera
quantity: largest difference, in milliseconds, of the sweep's crossing, entry and duration over the image from the geometry of a 10 Hz lidar (clockwise and counter-clockwise, phase 0° and 90°, turned round), level 6 mm pinhole cameras ahead, left and right, and one 2 m ahead looking left (parallax: it is crossed when the lidar faces atan(20 m / 2 m))
reference: the head's azimuth phase ∓ 360°·f·t written out in the check; the image's half field atan(2.88 mm / 6 mm)

title: Triggers centre the middle row's exposure on the sweep
quantity: largest difference of each camera's ideal trigger from its crossing − readout/2 − exposure/2 (modulo the period) and of its misalignment from zero, cameras alone on their lines, three readout and exposure times
reference: a rolling shutter's middle row is exposed around trigger + readout/2 + exposure/2 (Liang et al.)

title: Motion blur and rolling-shutter skew through the lens
quantity: largest relative difference of the image speed of a static object 5 m to the side at 36 km/h (level 6 mm pinhole) from f·v/d at the image centre and f·v/(d·cos α) in the corner, of the blur over a 2 ms exposure and the skew over a 20 ms readout from speed × time; and of a fisheye pitched down from v·sin(pitch)/d × its centre sampling (to 1 %)
reference: the angular rate v·sin β / d of a static point seen from a moving camera, through the lens, written out in the check

title: Sky blocked by a wall against its solid angle
quantity: largest relative difference of the share of the sky above the 10° mask a wall in front of a roof antenna hides (sky view on 0.5° × 0.5° cells) from the wall face's solid angle, four walls; the cells of an open roof must add up to the hemisphere and see all of it
reference: the solid angle of a rectangle seen from a point, integrated with scipy.integrate.quad

title: The pose error budget against a hand calculation and Monte Carlo
quantity: largest relative difference of a camera's position σ (3 m, 1 m and 1 m lever arm from the IMU) from the hand calculation INS σ ⊕ (δθ × L) ⊕ lever-arm σ, and of its attitude part from the spread of 400 000 sampled attitude errors crossed with the lever arm
reference: small-angle error propagation δp = δθ × L (Groves), by hand and by Monte Carlo

title: A unit calibration recovers a simulated unit's lens
quantity: RMS pixel distance, over the field out to 65° off the axis, between the lens fitted by calib.calibrate from 16 synthetic board views (rendered through a unit 1.5 % off the library focal length with an offset principal point, 2 grey levels of noise, half resolution) and that unit's true lens; the library lens must be at least 5 times further off, the focal length within 0.3 %
reference: the simulated unit's own intrinsics (the images are rendered from them)

title: The joint solve reaches the optimum of its least-squares problem
quantity: largest difference, in units of each parameter's 1σ, between the installation check's joint solve (joint.joint_solve from each camera's own PnP) and an independent Gauss–Newton solve of the same Huber problem, for simulated captures of the sample's six cameras and eight floor boards (corners with 0.5 px noise, boards laid off their plan by the placement prior, cameras off theirs by up to 1° and 10 mm); the Huber cost must not be higher than the reference's
reference: the same problem written out from scratch (own parameterisation, IRLS Gauss–Newton, central differences), solved to convergence

title: The joint solve recovers known poses from exact corners
quantity: largest error of the camera poses the joint solve gives from noise-free corners of the sample's boards, boards where planned, every camera mounted off its plan by up to 1° and 10 mm, in degrees (rotation) and millimetres (position)
reference: the injected poses the corners were rendered from

title: Predicted camera σ against the joint solve's spread
quantity: largest |log(empirical σ / predicted σ)| over every camera's and camera pair's six axes, the predicted σ of the observability study (Fisher information through the lens model) against the spread of the joint solve's answers to 200 simulated captures (the sample's six cameras, boards exact, 0.4 px corner noise); the tolerance is 4.5 standard errors of a σ estimated from the trials, and each camera's and pair's mean squared Mahalanobis distance must lie within 4 standard deviations of its degrees of freedom
reference: Monte Carlo solves with core.joint.joint_solve, the machinery that solves real captures

title: Predicted σ with boards laid by hand
quantity: largest |log(empirical σ / predicted σ)| over cameras F and ML and their pair, boards laid off their plan by draws of the placement σ (the joint solve's answers carried to the optimum of its least squares), 100 trials, tolerance 4.5 standard errors
reference: Monte Carlo solves with core.joint.joint_solve

title: Radar pose σ from corner reflectors
quantity: relative difference of the radar's x σ from σ_r / √n and of its (y, yaw) covariance from the inverse of the range–azimuth Fisher information Σ [[1/r², 1/r], [1/r, 1]] / σ_az² for three reflectors straight ahead; the Monte Carlo spread of a least-squares solve must agree (ratios 0.8–1.25 over 200 trials)
reference: the Fisher information of range and azimuth measurements, written out in the check; Monte Carlo

title: Predicted lidar–camera σ against the calibration's spread
quantity: largest |log(empirical σ / predicted σ)| over the six axes of the data rig's camera F – lidar L1 pair, the study's prediction against the spread of the lidar–camera calibration's own solve on simulated noisy corners and lidar points of the planned board poses, 60 trials, tolerance 4.5 standard errors
reference: Monte Carlo solves with core.lidar_calib._solve

title: Plane-to-plane alignment recovers a known transform
quantity: largest element difference between the transform the closed-form plane alignment gives for four exact board planes (seen by the camera and, through a known T_camera_lidar, by the lidar) and that T; two planes must not fix it
reference: the transform the planes were generated with

title: An injected lidar mounting error is recovered
quantity: position error (mm) of the lidar L1 the lidar–camera calibration recovers from synthetic captures (camera images through the real lens, lidar scans with range noise) of its six planned board poses with camera F, L1 mounted 15, −10, 8 mm and 0.6°, −0.4°, 0.3° off its plan; the rotation error must be under 0.08° and the error within 3 of the solve's own 1σ
reference: the injected mounting error the captures were simulated with

title: nuScenes calibrated_sensor rows
quantity: largest pixel distance between where a point lands through a camera's calibrated_sensor row (translation, the w-first sensor-to-ego quaternion transposed, camera_intrinsic and the Kannala–Brandt coefficients through cv2.fisheye) and where Vantage's lens model puts it, every camera, custom export origin
reference: the nuScenes devkit's convention (points into the sensor frame by −translation, then the rotation transposed); OpenCV's fisheye projection

title: KITTI calib_cam_to_cam and calib_cams_to_vehicle
quantity: largest pixel distance between where a point lands through KITTI's files (vehicle → camera 00 by the inverse of Tr_cam_00_to_vehicle, camera 00 → camera n by R_n, T_n, then K_n and D_n by the stated distortion model) and where Vantage's lens model puts it; P_rect_n must equal K_n [R_n | T_n]
reference: the KITTI raw devkit's (and pykitti's) reading of the files

title: ROS camera_info files
quantity: largest pixel distance between where a point (in the camera's optical frame, REP 103) lands through camera_matrix and distortion_coefficients by the stated distortion_model (equidistant through cv2.fisheye, plumb_bob through the pinhole) and where Vantage's lens model puts it; the projection matrix must be [K | 0] and the rectification the identity
reference: sensor_msgs/CameraInfo and the camera_calibration_parsers YAML layout; OpenCV

title: Kalibr camchain
quantity: largest pixel distance between where a point lands through each camera's Kalibr model (projected by the model's published equations, written for the check) and where Vantage's lens model puts it, for pinhole models; for a fitted wide-angle model (omni, double sphere, extended unified) the largest distance must not exceed the fit error the file states for it, and a fit outside the export's limits (0.25 px RMS, 1 px max) must carry its warning; T_cn_cnm1 must carry the previous camera's coordinates into this one (to 1 µm)
reference: the Kalibr camera models' equations (Mei & Rives; Usenko et al.; Khomutenko et al.; Kannala–Brandt) and Kalibr's camchain.yaml conventions

title: Sobol indices of the Ishigami function
quantity: largest difference of the first-order (Saltelli et al. 2010) and total (Jansen 1999) indices experiments.sobol_indices estimates from a scrambled Sobol sequence (8192 base samples, A, B and AB_i matrices) from the Ishigami function's analytic indices (a = 7, b = 0.1); every analytic index must lie in its 95 % bootstrap interval (a margin of 0.01 allowed for the bootstrap's own spread)
reference: the analytic Sobol indices of the Ishigami function

title: Morris elementary effects of a linear function
quantity: largest difference of the μ, μ* and σ experiments.morris_indices gives for y = Σ c_i x_i on the unit cube (20 random trajectories on a 4-level grid) from c_i, |c_i| and 0
reference: the elementary effects of a linear function, which are its coefficients exactly

title: Wilson's interval for a share
quantity: largest difference of experiments.wilson's 95 % and 90 % intervals for 0/10, 3/10, 17/40, 99/100 and 500/1000 from scipy.stats.binomtest's Wilson interval
reference: scipy.stats.binomtest(k, n).proportion_ci(method='wilson')

title: Uncertainty propagated through a linear function
quantity: relative difference of the standard deviation experiments.uncertainty gives for y = 2·x1 + 3·x2 − 1 with x1, x2 standard normal (20 000 draws) from the analytic √13, and of its mean from −1 in units of that σ; the analytic σ must lie in its bootstrap interval; tolerance 4.5 standard errors of a σ estimated from the draws
reference: the variance of a linear combination of independent normals, written out in the check

title: A frozen camera is found with its repeated frames
quantity: frames wrongly counted (missed or extra) by the drive-log check's freeze detector (content fingerprints, runs of images identical to the one before) on 300 frames of a still scene with sensor noise into which a stalled camera's repeats are written at known places (runs of 1, 3 and 10 repeats, one after a dropped frame; the same frames also as 0.8 MB raw payloads, fingerprinted by samples), checked against rig health's own frozen counter on the same frames
reference: the runs as written into the sequence; rig health's independent counter (pixel equality of the thumbnails)

title: Rig health judges the capture skew against the sync plan
quantity: largest difference, in milliseconds, of rig health's capture-time skew from the skew written into the capture times of three cameras of a lidar-synchronised rig (fired 25 and 75 ms after the front camera, as the sweep crosses them, with 0.4 ms of jitter): every camera on time, then the left one 7 ms late, then every camera fired together; and without the plan the stagger itself
reference: the trigger times of a clockwise 10 Hz lidar sweep written out in the check (the front camera at 0 ms, the right one at 25 ms, the left one at 75 ms)
